description: semanticCommits is pinned rather than left at its default of `auto`. Auto-detection infers the convention by reading recent commits on the default branch, and this repo was recreated in Aug 2026 from a single squashed commit (the 950-commit history is in edjeffreys/infrastructure-archive). With only `Initial commit` to look at, Renovate concluded the repo does not use conventional commits and silently dropped the `chore(deps):` prefix from every PR title. Stating it explicitly means the convention no longer depends on history that may be squashed again.

regexManagers.description: Runner image for the ARC scale set. The kubernetes manager only reads manifest-shaped files, and a Helm values file has no apiVersion/kind, so this image was invisible to Renovate and silently went five releases stale. GitHub then deprecated it, the runner exited 7, and ARC tore the scale set down in a loop.
kubeconform binary pinned in the manifest validation workflow.

Flux CLI pinned in the manifest validation workflow. Must track the controllers installed in-cluster: `flux build` renders with the CLI's own kustomize and API versions, so a CLI older than the cluster can pass a manifest the cluster then rejects.
yamllint version pinned in the manifest validation workflow.
Talos ISO version in Terraform. Must track talconfig.yaml: this is the image VMs boot in maintenance mode, and a stale one refuses configs built for a newer Kubernetes.
Talos installer version in the manual worker upgrade script.
Postgres image on CloudNativePG Clusters. The kubernetes manager only matches `image:` keys, so `imageName:` on a Cluster CR would otherwise never be bumped.

packageRules.description: The three Talos installer pins -- talconfig.yaml, terraform/proxmox/talos.tf and scripts/upgrade-workers.sh -- must move together or a rebuilt VM boots maintenance media that rejects the config. kubernetes/kubernetes used to be grouped here too; it was split out because grouping meant a Kubernetes minor rode along with every Talos patch, and the two are gated on different things. See the ceiling below.

Kubernetes cannot run ahead of what Cilium is e2e-tested against, and nothing tells Renovate that -- Cilium publishes its support matrix as prose in its docs, with no metadata any manager can read. Cilium 1.19 supports Kubernetes 1.31-1.34; 1.20 supports 1.33-1.36. The cluster is already past that on 1.36.1 with Cilium 1.19.2, which is why this ceiling is deliberately below the newest release rather than at it. Raise it only *after* Cilium is upgraded, never in the same PR: https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/network/kubernetes/requirements/

ARC chart updates are held back deliberately. The pattern stays unanchored on purpose. Under the old argocd manager the depName came out doubled — `.../gha-runner-scale-set/gha-runner-scale-set` — because that manager appends `chart:` to a repoURL already ending in the chart name, so an `^actions/` anchor never matched and Renovate retried the failing lookup every run. Since wave 14 these charts are read by the flux manager from flux/apps/arc-*.yaml, which builds the name differently again; matching on the substring keeps the hold-back working across both.

Plex runs the plex-postgresql shim image rather than plexinc/pms-docker directly (see kubernetes/plex/deployment.yaml). Its tags track the shim's version, not Plex's, so Plex updates arrive only when that project rebuilds.

claude-agent is built from images/claude-agent/Dockerfile by build-claude-agent.yaml and pushed as :latest (plus :sha-<short-sha>), so there is no upstream version for Renovate to track here. It also must not be caught by the pinDigests rule below: digest updates are disabled repo-wide, so a pinned digest would freeze the agent at whatever it was first pinned to. The Dockerfile's own ARG pins are still managed.

buildkitd runs in-cluster (kubernetes/buildkit/deployment.yaml, the -rootless variant) and build-claude-agent.yaml runs the matching buildctl client as its job container. Two managers see the two pins — kubernetes and github-actions — so without this they arrive as separate PRs and the client can be merged a release ahead of the daemon it talks to.
